questions.question: What is compressed yeast? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• What is compressed yeast? (CO2)
  • Compressed yeast is a moist, solid form of baker’s yeast containing about 70% moisture,
  • used as a biological leavening agent in bread fermentation.

questions.question: Define bread staling / [CO6]
questions.solution_html:
• Define bread staling. (CO6)
  • Bread staling is the process in which bread loses its freshness and softness over time due
  • to starch retrogradation and moisture redistribution.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Define rope disease in bread. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Define rope disease in bread. (CO3)
  • Rope disease is a bacterial spoilage of bread caused mainly by Bacillus species , resulting
  • in sticky, stringy crumb and a fruity odor.

questions.question: What is over-mixing of dough? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• What is over-mixing of dough? (CO2)
  • Over-mixing of dough occurs when mixing continues beyond optimal gluten development,
  • causing gluten breakdown and poor dough structure.

questions.question: What is creaming method / [CO6]
questions.solution_html:
• What is creaming method? (CO6)
  • The creaming method is a cake -mixing technique in which fat and sugar are beaten
  • together to incorporate air before adding eggs and flour.

questions.question: How would enzyme activity during fermentation influence the quality, volume, and texture of bread? Explain with suitable examples. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• How would enzyme activity during fermentation influence bread quality, volume and
  • texture? (CO2)
  • During fermentation, enzymes such as amylases convert starch into fermentable sugars.
  • Yeast uses these sugars to produce carbon dioxide and alcohol. The CO ₂ gas expands the
  • dough, increasing bread volume. Enzyme activity also improves crumb texture, softness,
  • flavor and crust color.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Write a detaited note on non- fermented baked foods. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Write a detailed note on non-fermented baked foods. (CO1)
  • Non-fermented baked foods are products that do not undergo yeast fermentation. Instead,
  • they may use chemical leavening agents or no leavening agents at all. Examples include
  • biscuits, cookies, crackers and certain cakes. These products rely on mixing, shaping and
  • baking processes to obtain their texture and structure.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe the quality characteristics of good biscuits and crackers and explain how they are evaluated. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the quality characteristics of good biscuits and crackers and how they are
  • evaluated. (CO4)
  • Good biscuits and crackers should h ave uniform shape, attractive color, pleasant aroma,
  • crisp texture and proper moisture content. Evaluation is done using sensory evaluation
  • (taste, aroma, appearance, texture), physical tests (thickness, spread ratio), and chemical
  • tests (moisture and fat content).
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the preparation of angel food cake. / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the preparation of angel food cake. (CO5)
  • Angel food cake is prepared mainly using egg whites. Egg whites are whipped to form
  • foam, sugar is gradually added, and flour is gently folded into the mixture. The batter is
  • poured into moulds and baked. The cake is cooled upside down to maintain its light and
  • airy structure.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

  • maintain gluten strength and bread quality.

questions.question: Explain time and temperature requirements for common baked products. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain time and temperature requirements for common baked products. (CO1)
  • Different baked products require specific baking temperatures and times. Bread is
  • typically baked at 200 –230°C for 25 –35 minutes. Cakes are baked at 160 –180°C, while
  • biscuits and cookies are usually baked at 180–220°C for shorter durations. Proper control
  • of time and temperature ensures good volume, crust color, texture and product quality.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Define leavening agents and explain their classification in detail. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Define leavening agents and explain their classification. (CO2)
  • Leavening agents are substances that produce gas in dough or batter, causing it to expand
  • and become light and porous. They are classified into:
  • • Biological leavening agents: Yeast
  • • Chemical leavening agents: Baking powder, baking soda
  • • Physical leavening agents: Air and steam.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Define fermentation in bread making. When does fermentation occur during processing, and examine the factors affecting it. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Define fermentation in bread making and factors affecting it. (CO3)
  • Fermentation in bread making is the process by which yeast converts sugars into carbon
  • dioxide and alcohol, causing the dough to rise. Fermentation occurs during dough resting
  • and proofing stages. Factors affecting fermentation include temperature, yeast quantity ,
  • sugar concentration, pH, dough consistency and fermentation time.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe different types of biscuits (soft dough, hard dough, fermented biscuits) and compare their manufacturing methods / [CO6] [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe different types of biscuits and compare their manufacturing methods.
  • (CO6)
  • Biscuits are commonly classified into soft dough biscuits, hard dough biscuits and
  • fermented biscui ts.Soft dough biscuits contain higher fat and sugar and require less
  • gluten development. Hard dough biscuits have lower fat and sugar and involve stronger
  • gluten formation. Fermented biscuits undergo dough fermentation before baking. Their
  • manufacturing me thods differ mainly in dough preparation, fermentation and sheeting
  • processes.
